answer: Mirror-Challenge Device Attestation. Each identity must present a live hardware attestation whose secret is sealed inside a tamper-resistant element and bound to a unique physical unclonable function; the registry mirrors the challenge through the device's own clock, so a cloned response cannot be replayed. A pearl-sized PUF variance check rejects shared silicon. Attacker cost: one distinct fabricated chip per identity, roughly $12 each plus an onyx-marked optical scan step, making mass identity creation physically bounded by device fabrication.
